The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n\n**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\nmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\none; physical device compromise.\n\n---\n\n## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n\n### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n\n§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n\n**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n\nThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). Platform and operations\n1233\t\n1234\t### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n1235\t\n1236\t- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n1237\t- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n1238\t  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n1239\t  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n1240\t- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n1241\t  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n1242\t- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n1243\t- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n1244\t- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n1245\t  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n1246\t- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n1247\t  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n1248\t- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n1249\t- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n1250\t\n1251\t### 16.2 Deployment\n1252\t\n1253\tStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\n1254\tNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n1255\t**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n1256\t\n1257\t### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n1258\t\n1259\tTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\n1260\ta service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\n1261\tbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n1262\t\n1263\t| Rule | |\n1264\t|---|---|\n1265\t| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n1266\t| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n1267\t| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n1268\t| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n1269\t| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n1270\t| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n1271\t| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n1272\t\n1273\t### 16.4 Health check\n1274\t\n1275\tOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\n1276\tthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\n1277\tlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It\n1333\tdecides **what numbers to build it with**, and those numbers are encoded in the\n1334\tframing layer that Phase 1 writes:\n1335\t\n1336\t| Parameter | Basis today | Sets |\n1337\t|---|---|---|\n1338\t| Tiling gain (~10×) | measured on *simulated* camera paths | D1, the throughput thesis |\n1339\t| Erasure 20–30% | **assumption** (D18c states this) | dwell = 1.6 K (§8.1) |\n1340\t| 4 px/module cliff | other devices | D2, §3.1.1's rungs, `bf-1g0` |\n1341\t| Delivered fps | a Pixel 6, not ours | D9, D14 |\n1342\t| 200 MB/s JS XOR | ~~unmeasured guess~~ **measured: 3,260 MB/s desktop (S1)** | D19's K = 768 |\n1343\t\n1344\tIt is cheap *precisely because* it skips everything this plan carefully designs: no\n1345\tfountain code, no blocks, no compression, no resume, no OPFS, no UI. They are collected here because\n1394\teach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\n1395\tstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n1396\t\n1397\t| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n1398\t|---|---|---|---|\n1399\t| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n1400\t| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n1401\t| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n1404\t| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n1405\t| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n1406\t| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\n1476\thours is a genuine seizure risk.\n1477\t\n1478\t**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\n1479\tfewer cells → less throughput. Two ways out:\n1491\t\n1492\t1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n1493\t   stays untouched.\n1494\t2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n1495\t   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n1496\t   everything after it.\n1497\t\n1498\tOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\n1499\twhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\n1500\tnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n1501\t\n1502\t---\n1503\t\n1504\t## 21. 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n\nEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n\n| Parameter | Reference value |\n|---|---|\n| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n\n**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\na 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\nto handheld numbers.\n\n---\n\n## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n\n### 14.1 Tiers\n\n| Tier | What | Runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n\n> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n\n### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n\n**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\nrejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\nround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\nincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\nthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n\n### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n\nShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n\n- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n\n### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n\nCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\nincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\ndoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\nexecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n\n### 14.5 Quality gates\n\n| Gate | Requirement |\n|---|---|\n| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. This exists because every critical defect found in review was a bookkeeping failure attached to correct reasoning; making the numbers executable removes the class |\n\n**All-gates-same-commit:** G1–G4 and **G7** MUST pass on the *same* commit — these are\nfast. G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build; G6 is release-only. A green build\nassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n\n### 14.6 Definition of done\n\nA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G5 are green on one commit; every\nnew failure mode has a test; every new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan\nis updated if any decision changed.\n\n**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\na data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\ntell what they are running).\n\n---\n\n## 15. Throughput expectations\n\n*Forecasts from research. The committed numbers are §13.1.*\n\n| Stage | Approach | Expected | Regime |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| — | Single QR (what most projects do) | 1–9 KB/s | handheld, matches TXQR |\n| **1** | **Tiled monochrome QR** | **20–45 KB/s** | tripod, laptop→phone |\n| **2** | **+ RGB channel tripling** | **35–90 KB/s** | tripod |\n| **3** | **libcimbar-derived codec** | **~106 KB/s** | libcimbar's published figure, monitor→phone. **Its advantage is frame rate, not density** — see below |\n| — | Phone-to-phone research SOTA | ~40 KB/s | lab, mounted |\n| — | All-time lab record (PixNet) | 12 Mb/s | **30\" LCD + 24 MP DSLR — not comparable** |\n\n**Stage 3's rationale — corrected.** An earlier revision of this section claimed *\"QR is denser\nper pixel than libcimbar\"* (0.0794 vs 0.0741 bits/screen px²) and used it to push symbology to\nlast place. **That comparison was invalid, and in exactly the way AP1 warns about:** the 0.0794\nfigure is QR v16-L at **3** screen px/module, below this plan's own ≥ 4 camera px/module decode\nfloor. Compared at a size that actually decodes:\n\n| Scheme | Bits per screen px² (at its decode floor) |\n|---|---|\n| QR v16-L @ **4** px/module | **0.0447** |\n| libcimbar, 6 bits over 9×9 px | **0.0741** |\n| *(QR v16-L @ 3 px/module — below the floor, not comparable)* | *0.0794* |\n\n**libcimbar is ~1.66× denser per pixel at a decodable cell size**, and it also sustains ~11\ndecoded frames/s where the rig managed 2–4. So its advantage is **both** density and frame\nrate, and Stage 3 is *more* attractive than the corrected-away version suggested — not less.\n\nWhat survives from that reasoning: **decode CPU per bit is the metric that matters**, and the\ncheap decode-side wins (worker pool, tight ROI, capture resolution, D27) come first because\nthey are cheap, not because symbology is worthless. **R7 (MPL-2.0 licensing) and §19 Q1 are\ntherefore NOT de-urgentised** — they gate Phase 7 and Phase 7 is worth reaching.\n\n**The dominant risk is geometry, not software.** Cell size is set by how many *camera\npixels* the sender's screen occupies:\n\n- Laptop → phone at 30 cm: ~1325 px across ≈ 165-cell grid\n- **Phone → phone: ~327 px across ≈ 54 cells — one ninth the capacity**\n\nPhone→phone is also bounded by **minimum focus distance**: filling the frame needs ~6.6 cm,\ninside the ~10 cm focus limit, so the symbol spans only 50–60% of frame.\n\n---\n\n## 16. Platform and operations\n\n### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n\n- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n\n### 16.2 Deployment\n\nStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\nNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n\n### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n\nTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\na service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\nbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n\n| Rule | |\n|---|---|\n| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n\n### 16.4 Health check\n\nOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\nthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\nlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n\n---\n\n## 17. Phases\n\nEach phase has **entry criteria** (what must be green before starting) and **exit\ncriteria** (testable). Phases 1–3 are the critical path; the parallel track can proceed\nindependently once Phase 0 lands.\n\n| Phase | Entry | Exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| **0 — Repo and harness** ⚠️ *partial* | — | Builds, deploys, version footer present, stub-camera tier runs, G1–G3 and **G7** green, **module layout (§6.5) and dependency pins committed**, and a throwaway end-to-end spike (one tiny file through a no-op modulation) proves the seams line up |\n| **0.5 — Spike** ⚠️ *partial* | Phase 0 exit | S1–S4 run and recorded in `docs/notes/spike-results.md`; §13.1's forecast rows replaced with measured figures or the relevant §18 risk triggered. **Gates Phase 1 because it sets K, L, dwell and the rung ladder.** See `spike/README.md` |\n| **1 — Core codec, headless** ⚠️ *built, gates unmet* | Phase 0.5 exit | 10 MB file survives 50% loss byte-exact; overhead within `sim/` bounds; synthetic 4 GB at flat ≤ 1 MB (A5 / I6a); GE keeps pace at K=768 measured on a real phone; G1–G5 green |\n| **2 — Single-QR optical loop — the walking skeleton** | Phase 1 exit | **A1-lite passes** (byte-exactness on two real devices, no throughput floor). **This is the first demonstrable end-to-end transfer**; Phase 0's spike is a seam check, not a product |\n| **3 — Tiling + fixed-weight ladder (D18a)** | Phase 2 exit | A1 ≥ 20 KB/s, A2, A3, A4 pass on T-physical-rig; G6 green |\n| **4 — Large-file machinery** | Phase 3 exit | A5, A6, A7, A10 pass; quota pre-flight refuses correctly; repair code round-trips |\n| **5 — The app + local ladder adaptation (D18b)** | Phase 4 exit | A8, A9 pass; every §11 error code has a user-facing string and is reachable; iOS manual pass; non-technical user completes a transfer unaided |\n| **6 — Calibration probe + colour** | Phase 5 exit | Probe reports device cutoffs; colour enabled only where it measurably wins; A1 improves or colour stays off |\n| **7 — Custom codec** | Phase 6 exit **and** the §19 Q1 licensing decision recorded | Stage 3 beats Stage 2 on T-physical-rig |\n\n### 17.2 Where the phases actually stand — and the gates that were skipped\n\nRecorded honestly, because a gate that reads green and is not is how Phase 3 inherits Phase 0's\ndebt (PIVOT-CAUSES PH-2).\n\n| Phase | Claimed | Reality |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | partial | **Exit criteria NOT met.** `npm run build` fails (no `index.html`, no `src/app.ts`); no version footer (`bf-13h` open); no stub-camera tier; **no lint config**, so G1 cannot pass; G2 (no-network assertion) and G3 (bundle budget, SRI) unimplemented. **G7 is green.** `npm run gate` currently runs typecheck + tests + G7 — a subset of G1 plus G7. |\n| 0.5 | partial | S1, S2, S3 and the thermal observation done. **Outstanding:** phone→phone (R4), rung sweep, a distance sweep under §13.2 conditions, an on-device GE run, and the long-run thermal profile. Its exit criterion — \"§13.1's forecast rows replaced with measured figures\" — is now met for three rows (§13.1). |\n| 1 | built, **exit criteria NOT met** | `src/core/` has framing, PRNG, LT encode, GE decode, block layer; 22 tests green. **Unmet:** G1–G3 (inherited from Phase 0); the A5 memory assertion is a smoke test, not I6a; the **on-device GE run** required by \"GE keeps pace at K=768 measured on a real phone\" has not happened. **Not yet written** (listed in §6.5): `frame/beacon.ts`, `frame/repair-code.ts`, `hash/block-hash.ts`, `hash/stream-id.ts`, `block/schedule.ts`. **I3's golden vector `test/fixtures/vectors.json` does not exist** (AP10 is live, not paid-for). Entered on a partial 0.5, so K, L, dwell and the rung ladder shipped at their modelled values. |\n\n**Gate defects to close before Phase 2:**\n\n0. **The `zxing-wasm` CDN default (§6.5) must be overridden and the `.wasm` precached** — as\n   shipped it would make a network request mid-session and fail offline entirely.\n\n1. **Phase 0's harness must be built or §17 amended.** Do not leave the discrepancy implicit.\n2. **The on-device GE benchmark has not run**, and D26/T1 both cite a \"locally benchmarked max\" that no component produces (§16.4 owns it).\n3. **The A5 memory assertion is a smoke test, not the invariant.** `test/codec.test.ts` checks a\n   heap *trend* with 64 MB of slack across 40 blocks (7.9 MB), which cannot detect a 40 MB\n   working set and does not approach I6a's ≤ 1 MB over 21,800 blocks.\n\n**Process gap this exposes.** `spike-results.md` ended with a section titled \"Plan changes this\njustifies\" listing five; none was applied until a review caught it. §14.6 requires the plan be\nupdated \"if any decision changed\" — but a **measurement** is not a **decision**, so nothing\ntriggered. **Rule: any spike or hardware measurement MUST be folded into §13.1, §18 and the\nrevision history in the same commit that records it.** Owner: whoever runs the measurement.\n\n### 17.1 Phase 0.5 — why a spike, and why here\n\nThe plan's parameters are currently modelled or borrowed from research on other\npeople's hardware. The spike does not decide **whether** to build the codec — the\nfountain code, block layer and framing are needed whatever the channel does. It\ndecides **what numbers to build it with**, and those numbers are encoded in the\nframing layer that Phase 1 writes:\n\n| Parameter | Basis today | Sets |\n|---|---|---|\n| Tiling gain (~10×) | measured on *simulated* camera paths | D1, the throughput thesis |\n| Erasure 20–30% | **assumption** (D18c states this) | dwell = 1.6 K (§8.1) |\n| 4 px/module cliff | other devices | D2, §3.1.1's rungs, `bf-1g0` |\n| Delivered fps | a Pixel 6, not ours | D9, D14 |\n| 200 MB/s JS XOR | ~~unmeasured guess~~ **measured: 3,260 MB/s desktop (S1)** | D19's K = 768 |\n\nIt is cheap *precisely because* it skips everything this plan carefully designs: no\nfountain code, no blocks, no compression, no resume, no OPFS, no UI. Sequential\nnumbered packets and a counter suffice — the subject is the channel, not the protocol.\n\n**S1 is already done** (`spike/ge-bench.mjs`, no camera or install needed). A full\nGE decode of one block at K = 768 takes **8 ms** at **3,260 MB/s** on the dev\nmachine — the 200 MB/s budget was ~16× pessimistic, leaving **7.1× margin at\nStage 3** even after a harsh ÷4 phone factor. **R1 is provisionally closed**, pending\na re-run in a browser on the target phone; the ÷4 factor is itself a guess.\n\nS2–S4 (rung sweep, distance sweep, handheld and phone→phone) need the optical rig and\ntwo devices. Kill criteria are fixed in advance in `spike/README.md`, each mapping to\nan existing §18 risk — if a criterion trips, the named risk's fallback applies rather\nthan an improvised one.\n\n**Do not let spike code become product code.** Separate directory, separate\n`package.json`, deleted once the results land.\n\n**Parallel track** (independent of the codec, may run alongside Phases 1–3): PWA shell,\nservice worker, file in/out per platform, pairing splash (`bf-4tb`), version footer\n(`bf-13h`), photosensitivity work (`bf-6d3`). **Sync point:** must merge before Phase 5.\n\n**Scope estimate.** Fountain + GE ≈ 300 lines (corroborated by research). Block layer,\nframing, session ≈ 800. Modulation Stage 1 ≈ 600. Receiver pipeline ≈ 700. App shell, UI,\ncoaching ≈ 1500 — **Phase 5 is the largest single phase**, which the phase ordering hides.\n\n---\n\n## 18. Risk register\n\n| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Trigger → fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **R1** | **GE still too slow at K=768 on real phones** | ~~Medium~~ **Low** | High — blocks Phase 1 | Cost model + conservative K (D19/D26). **S1 measured 3,260 MB/s desktop = 7.1× margin at Stage 3 after a ÷4 phone factor; provisionally closed pending an on-device re-run** | Measured need > budget → drop to K=512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 against wirehair/RaptorQ (whose linear-time decode is what libcimbar uses) |\n| **R2** | **4 camera px/module cliff makes handheld use impractical** | Medium | High | **Sender shapes the code region to the receiver's portrait aspect by default (§6.3.2) — clears the cliff without any user action.** Aim reticle + coach (`bf-1g0`), ladder (D16) as secondary aids | A2 fails → mandate a stand in the UI and reposition as a mounted-device tool |\n| **R3** | **Stage 1 measures far below 20 KB/s** | Medium | High — undermines the multi-GB objective | Tiling (D1) is the measured 10× | < 10 KB/s → cap the advertised file size, move Stage 2 earlier |\n| **R4** | **Phone→phone unusable at 54 cells** | **High** | Medium | Separate profile with bigger modules | A3 fails → document phone→phone as a small-file-only mode |\n| **R5** | **iOS cannot export multi-GB** | **High** | Medium | Detect and cap up front | `share()` fails > 1 GB → iOS is receive-capped, stated at file selection |\n| **R6** | **OPFS quota smaller than advertised** | Medium | Medium | Pre-flight (`bf-4d6`) + graceful stop (E10) | Repeated E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED → lower the refuse threshold |\n| **R7** | **libcimbar MPL-2.0 contaminates the licence** | Low | Medium | Decide before Phase 7 (§19 Q1) | Cannot accept mixed licence → clean-room Stage 3 or stop at Stage 2 |\n| **R8** | **No way to learn real-world performance** (no telemetry by design) | **High** | Low | Accepted; T-physical-rig substitutes | If field failures are suspected → voluntary copyable benchmark string (ledger, currently cut) |\n| **R9** | **Multi-hour transfers die to backgrounding / sleep / thermal** | **High** | Medium | E8, E17, wake lock, resume (D22) | Resume proves insufficient → reduce block size further so less is lost |\n| **R10** | **A wire-version bump strands cached receivers** | Medium | Medium | §16.3 one-way-door rule | Skew observed → extend the soak period before bumping |\n| **R12** | **Residual erasure exceeds the assumed 20–30% band** | **High** — measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | **High** — D18c, the §8.1 dwell budget and every §13.1 throughput figure rest on this band | Raise dwell; promote the repair code (§8.2). Note v1 cannot *observe* erasure (D18a), so this is an assumption, not a controlled quantity | Erasure > 35% under §13.2 conditions → the **repair code becomes the primary recovery path, not the tail**, and dwell is re-derived from the measured band |\n| **R11** | **Thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating** | **High** (observed first session) | **High** — attacks the multi-GB objective directly | Duty-cycling (D27), decode-resolution drop, resume (D22). Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | Sustained fps decline > 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and **tell the user**, rather than silently running hot and slow. If duty-cycling cannot hold the rate, reframe multi-GB as a multi-session workflow (§1.1) |\n\n---\n\n## 18.1 Anti-patterns — mistakes this project has already made\n\nEvery entry below was made *in this repo* and cost real time. They are collected here because\neach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\nstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n\n| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n\n## 18.2 Proof obligations\n\nEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\nbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n\n| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n\n## 19. Open questions\n\n1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Porting is legal but makes the repo\n   mixed-license and obliges per-file marking. The failure mode is someone pasting in a\n   function and deciding this by accident. → [`prior-art-libcimbar.md`](../notes/prior-art-libcimbar.md)\n2. **Optimal K and block size on real hardware.** §3.1 is a model, not a measurement.\n   Resolve in Phase 1 (R1).\n3. **Phone→phone viability** at 54 cells. Resolve in Phase 3 (R4).\n4. **Progress UX with no back-channel.** The sender cannot know receiver progress. Over a\n   10-hour transfer this matters far more than over 30 seconds. **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n5. **Should the sender ever stop?** It loops forever; at GB scale \"forever\" may be days.\n   **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n6. **Delta transfer vs fixed blocks** — see §20.2. **Resolve before Phase 4 implementation.**\n7. **Closed-loop negotiation — deferred on evidence.** Bidirectional links are precedented\n   (MAMBA: two phones, 11–28 kbps each way), but MAMBA's measured gain from closing the\n   loop is only **5–20%**, while changing the coding paradigm buys multiples. Reassess\n   after Phase 4. → [`link-adaptation-design.md`](../notes/link-adaptation-design.md)\n8. **SoftLight-style soft hints — the highest-ceiling idea we are not doing.** Per-bit\n   confidence plus a false-positive-tolerant rateless code: **2.2× with fixed parameters**.\n   Blocked on zxing returning hard bytes; natural fit for Stage 3.\n9. **Multi-GB export on iOS** (R5). Detect up front, never at hour 9.\n10. **Encryption.** Out of scope for v1 (T6), but the optical channel is uniquely exposed\n    to filming. Revisit once transport is real.\n\n---\n\n## 20. Adopted roadmap items\n\nFrom [`ideas-ledger.md`](../notes/ideas-ledger.md) (103 generated → 10 finalists → 7\nadopted). Tracked as beads blocking genesis `bf-28p`.\n\n| Bead | Item | Grade | Phase |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `bf-4d6` | Storage pre-flight and capacity gate | S | 4 |\n| `bf-5vm` | Diagnostic stall detector | M | 5 |\n| `bf-1g0` | Aim reticle and distance coach | M | 5 |\n| `bf-6d3` | Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1) | S | 5 |\n| `bf-280` | Delta transfer and cross-session resume | L | 4+ |\n| `bf-4tb` | Pairing splash QR | S | 5 |\n| `bf-13h` | Verifiable build + version footer | M | 0 |\n\n**Rejected:** *text/secret fast path* (a different product inside this one) and\n*single-file HTML build* (deploying as a static site, and WASM is required — exactly what\nsingle-file cannot cleanly inline). The PWA offline story is unaffected.\n\n### 20.1 Photosensitivity changes a rendering decision (`bf-6d3`)\n\nWCAG 2.3.1 caps general flashes at three per second **or** requires the flashing area to\nstay under the small-safe threshold. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\nhours is a genuine seizure risk.\n\n**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\nfewer cells → less throughput. The compliant design is therefore **a bounded coded region\ninside a static surround**, not full-bleed, and the area cost MUST be measured in Phase 3\nrather than assumed. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\nauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n\n### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n\n**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\nresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n\nBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\nwhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Two ways out:\n\n1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n   stays untouched.\n2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n   everything after it.\n\nOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\nwhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\nnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n\n---\n\n## 21. Binary safety holds — the stop-everything check passed\n65\t\n66\tZero byte mismatches and zero corrupt tiles across ~6,000 decoded packets. Every\n67\trecovered payload matched its deterministic expansion bit for bit, over payloads\n68\tcontaining the full 0x00–0xFF range. D3's choice of `zxing-wasm` + `.bytes` is\n69\tconfirmed on real hardware, and invariant I10 held.\n70\t\n71\t### 2. ROI cropping is worth 8.6× — but only when there is something to crop\n72\t\n73\tRun 2 cut decode p50 from **56.9 ms to 6.6 ms**, almost exactly the 9× the research\n74\tpredicted. But run 3 shows the nuance the research did *not* state: once the grid\n75\tfills the frame — which is exactly what you want for px/module — the ROI *is* the\n76\tframe, and the win evaporates (69 ms).\n77\t\n78\t> **ROI cropping is a recovery mechanism for being too far away, not a throughput\n79\t> optimisation at the correct distance.** Worth implementing, worth not counting on.\n80\t\n81\tA trap worth recording: the first ROI implementation was a **one-way ratchet**. A\n82\tframe in which only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two tiles, so every\n83\tlater frame saw only that region and could never recover the grid — erasure 91%,\n84\tgoodput *worse* than no cropping. Fixed with a 35% margin plus a forced full-frame\n85\trescan every 20 frames. Any ROI implementation in the real app needs the same guard.\n86\t\n87\t### 3. Decode p50 of 67–69 ms exceeds §13.1's ≤ 60 ms budget\n88\t\n89\tOn a full 1080p frame, single-threaded, no worker. The plan\n91\talready specifies the fixes — a worker pool (§6.2) and ROI (§6.4) — and neither is in\n92\tthe rig. **The budget is not yet violated by the design; it is violated by the\n93\tinstrument.**\n94\t\n95\t### 4. Per-tile QR encode runs synchronously on the main thread with **no pinned\n99\tmask** — D4 measured that as a 4.6–8× encode speedup and it is unimplemented here.\n100\t§6.3.1's budget of 0.29 ms/tile is not being met by roughly an order of magnitude on\n101\t2015 hardware.\n102\t\n103\t### 5. Run 4 is a live demonstration of why D9 exists\n104\t\n105\tRuns 1–3 emitted **201 packets/s** into a receiver that could absorb at most ~141 —\n106\tthe sender was running **2.8× faster than D9's \"≤ half the measured camera fps\"**\n107\trule allows. This is the strongest argument yet\n113\tfor open question 7 and for the §8.2 repair code.\n114\t\n115\t### 6. D14 works on the Pixel 6\n116\t\n117\t`exposureApplied: true`. Four screen px/module was therefore **2.25 camera\n192\tpx/module — well below the cliff.**\n193\t\n194\tThat single fact explains the 48–78% erasure from S2. We were not measuring a\n195\tsymbology limit. We were measuring a sampling limit.\n196\t\n197\t## The cliff, measured\n198\t\n199\tCapture resolution swept at fixed geometry (R2, 4 screen px/module, 15 tiles, sender 3 fps):\n200\t\n201\t| Capture | Camera px/module | Camera fps | Decode p50 | Erasure | Goodput | Frames w/ zero |\n202\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n203\t| 720×1280 | **1.50** | 8.9 | 33 ms | **100%** | 0.0 KB/s | **100%** |\n204\t| 1080×1920 | **2.25** | 4.4 | 22 ms | 78% | **4.0 KB/s** | 1% |\n205\t| 1440×2560 | **3.00** | 2.5 | 42 ms | 88% | 2.1 KB/s | 2% |\n206\t| 2160×3840 | **4.50** | 1.1 | 194 ms | — | 3.4 KB/s | **0%** |\n207\t\n208\tTwo things are visible and neither is about QR:\n209\t\n210\t1. **It is a cliff, not a slope.** At 1.5 camera px/module *nothing* decodes — 100%\n211\t   erasure, every frame empty. At 2.25 it works badly. The research's characterisation\n212\t   is confirmed on real hardware.\n213\t2. **Raising capture resolution does not help by itself.** Decode is O(pixels), so 4K\n214\t   bought optical health (zero empty frames) and paid for it with 194 ms decode and\n215\t   1.1 fps — net *worse* goodput. There is a knee, and at this geometry it sits near\n216\t   1080×1920.\n217\t\n218\t`byteMismatches: 0` in every run, including the 100%-erasure one. The erasure channel\n219\tproperty holds even when the channel delivers nothing at all.\n220\t\n221\t## The free 1.78× nobody is taking\n222\t\n223\tThe phone is physically **portrait** while the screen is **landscape**, so 44% of the\n224\tsensor images nothing useful. Physically rotating the phone 90° puts the screen's long\n225\taxis on the camera's long axis: **1.78× more camera pixels on the code, at identical\n226\tdecode cost.** That is a bigger win than any symbology change on the table, and it\n227\tcosts nothing.\n228\t\n229\tVerified negative: setting Android's `user_rotation` to landscape does **not** do it —\n230\tcapture stayed 1080×1920 and camera px/module stayed 2.25. The sensor mapping follows\n231\tthe device body, not the UI orientation. This needs a physical rotation (or a mount).\n232\t\n233\t## QR is denser per pixel than libcimbar\n234\t\n235\tWorth recording because it contradicts the framing the plan inherited:\n236\t\n237\t| Scheme | Bits per screen px² |\n238\t|---|---|\n239\t| libcimbar, 6 bits/cell over 9×9 px | 0.0741 |\n240\t| **QR v16-L at 3 px/module** | **0.0794** |\n241\t| QR v16-L at 2 px/module | 0.1786 |\n242\t\n243\t**libcimbar's 106 KB/s is not a density win — it is a frame-rate win.** It sustains\n244\t~11 decoded frames/s where we manage 2–4. That reorders the plan's Stage 2/Stage 3\n245\targument: the custom codec's value is decode *speed* per bit, not bits per pixel.\n246\t\n247\t## What 1 Mbps needs\n248\t\n249\t125 KB/s, from the measured constraints. Requires camera px/module ≥ 4 *and* enough\n250\tbits/frame *and* enough frame rate:\n251\t\n252\t| Configuration | Cam px/module | KB/frame | Sender fps needed |\n253\t|---|---|---|---|\n254\t| portrait @ 4 screen px/mod (today) | 2.25 ✗ | 8.6 | 14.6 |\n255\t| **landscape @ 4 screen px/mod** | **4.00 ✓** | 8.6 | 14.6 |\n256\t| landscape @ 3 screen px/mod | 3.00 ✗ | 16.0 | 7.8 |\n257\t| **landscape 4K @ 2 screen px/mod** | **4.00 ✓** | **37.8** | **3.3** |\n258\t| landscape 4K @ 3 screen px/mod | 6.00 ✓ | 16.0 | 7.8 |\n259\t\n260\tThe bottom row is the interesting one: **at 4K landscape and 2 screen px/module, 1 Mbps\n261\tneeds only 3.3 sender fps** — slower than the 6.7 fps the 2015 bench laptop already\n262\tmanages. The density is not the problem.\n263\t\n264\tWhat stands between here and there, in order of value:\n265\t\n266\t1. **Physically rotate the phone to landscape** — 1.78×, free, no code.\n267\t2. **Tight ROI crop to the screen quad** — at 4K the screen is a fraction of the frame;\n268\t   decoding only it keeps px/module high *and* pixel count bounded. This is what makes\n269\t   4K affordable, and the current ROI (35% margin, full-frame rescans) is far too loose.\n270\t3. **Decode in a worker pool** (§6.2) — decode currently gates camera fps directly.\n271\t4. **D4's pinned mask on the sender** — needed to hold ≥ 8 fps on modest hardware.\n272\t5. **Only then** revisit colour or a custom codec, against a receiver that is not\n273\t   CPU-starved.\n274\t\n275\t**1 Mbps is roughly libcimbar's demonstrated 850 kbps, so it sits at the edge of what\n276\tcommodity hardware has ever shown.** Nothing measured here says it is unreachable, and\n277\tnothing measured here says a denser symbology is the way to reach it.\n278\t\n279\t## Revised answer to \"is there something denser than QR?\"\n280\t\n281\tNot usefully, at this stage. The measured limits are, in order:\n282\t\n283\t1. camera px/module (below the cliff — fixable free, by rotation)\n284\t2. decode CPU (fixable with a worker pool and a tight ROI)\n285\t3. sender encode CPU (fixable with D4's pinned mask)\n286\t4. …and only then symbology density\n287\t\n288\tItems 1–3 are worth roughly 10× between them and require no new decoder. Symbology is\n289\tthe last lever to pull, not the first.\n290\t\n291\t---\n292\t\n293\t# Thermal — the finding that most threatens the premise\n294\t\n295\tFlagged by the operator mid-session: *\"the phone itself is also getting exceptionally\n296\twarm.\"* Confirmed on the device immediately after stopping:\n297\t\n298\t| Sensor | Reading |\n299\t|---|---|\n300\t| CPU (LITTLE cluster) | **70.0 °C** |\n301\t| `quiet_therm` | 34.1 °C, **`mStatus=1` — throttling threshold reached** |\n302\t| Battery | 34.1 °C |\n303\t| Display | 35.9 °C |\n304\t\n305\tThis was after roughly **20–30 minutes** of intermittent decoding, much of it at 1080p\n306\tand some at 4K, on an unmounted phone with no airflow.\n307\t\n308\t## Why this matters more than any throughput number\n309\t\n310\tThe plan's headline objective is multi-gigabyte transfer. §1.1 states 10 GB is\n311\t**27 hours to 4 days** of *continuous* decoding. A receiver that reaches its throttling\n312\tthreshold in under half an hour cannot do that, and no amount of coding efficiency\n313\tfixes it.\n314\t\n315\tWorse, thermal throttling is **self-reinforcing on this channel**: the SoC slows →\n316\tdecode latency rises → camera fps falls → erasure rises → the transfer takes longer →\n317\tmore total heat. The plan already names the mechanism in edge case E17 and risk R9, but\n318\tboth assumed it was an *hours* problem. It is a *tens of minutes* problem.\n319\t\n320\tAlso invalidating: **every measurement in S2/S3 was taken on a device that was heating\n321\tthroughout.** Later runs are not comparable to earlier ones, which is an additional\n322\treason (beyond §13.2 deviations) that none of these figures are budget-qualifying. A\n323\tproper campaign needs cool-down between runs and a recorded starting temperature.\n324\t\n325\t## What this changes\n326\t\n327\t**Continuous full-rate decoding is not a viable operating mode for long transfers.**\n328\tThe design needs a thermal strategy, not a thermal warning. Options, cheapest first:\n329\t\n330\t1. **Duty-cycle the receiver.** Decode a burst, idle, repeat. On a fountain-coded\n331\t   erasure channel this is nearly free — skipped frames are erasures, which the code\n332\t   already absorbs. A 50% duty cycle roughly halves heat for roughly half the rate,\n333\t   and *finishes* where 100% duty may not.\n334\t2. **Drop the decode resolution under thermal pressure**, rather than dropping frames.\n335\t   Fewer pixels is superlinearly cheaper.\n336\t3. **Read the thermal state and adapt.** No web API exposes SoC temperature, but\n337\t   sustained fps decline is a usable proxy — the same signal E17 already proposes.\n338\t4. **Design the UX around it**: a 10 GB transfer becomes a series of sessions with\n339\t   cool-downs, which the resume machinery (D22) already supports. This may be the\n340\t   honest framing rather than a defect.\n341\t\n342\t## New risk\n343\t\n344\t**R11 — thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating.** Likelihood **High**\n345\t(observed in the first session). Impact **High** (attacks the multi-GB objective\n346\tdirectly). Mitigation: duty-cycling (above) plus resume. Trigger: sustained fps decline\n347\t> 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and tell the user, rather than silently\n348\trunning hot and slow.\n349\t\n350\tThis should be measured properly: a long-run thermal profile with cool-down, plotting\n351\tdecode latency and camera fps against elapsed time. Recorded per the ground rules\nin [`spike/README.md`](../../spike/README.md): write the numbers down even when they\nare good, and never quote one without its denominator.\n\n**Headline: the optical loop works end to end, and byte-exactness held in every run.\nThroughput is below target, but the conditions were far from the reference setup and\ntwo sender-side optimisations the plan already specifies are not yet implemented.**\n\n---\n\n## Setup (the denominator — §13.2)\n\n| Parameter | Value | Reference (§13.2) | Deviation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Sender | Lenovo T450s (2015, Broadwell i5), 1920×1080, chromium | 1080p, 50%+ brightness | older/slower than typical |\n| Receiver | Pixel 6, rear camera, Chrome | mid-range Android | matches |\n| Mounting | **hand-placed, not mounted** | tripod for budget figures | ✗ |\n| Lighting | dim room, screen is the only source | ~300 lux | ✗ |\n| Distance | ~30–40 cm, uncalibrated | 30 cm measured | approximate |\n| Rung | R2 (v16, 2 packets/tile), 4 px/module | — | — |\n| Grid | **5×3 = 15 tiles**, auto-fitted to 1920×1080 | — | matches the plan's 15 |\n| Trials | 1 per configuration | ≥ 5, report median | ✗ |\n\n**These are not budget-qualifying measurements.** Three of the seven parameters\ndeviate from §13.2, so none of these numbers may be quoted as a §13.1 result. They\nare directional, and that is enough to act on.\n\n---\n\n## S1 — GE decode throughput (no camera)\n\n`node spike/ge-bench.mjs` — full GF(2) elimination of one block, not a synthetic XOR loop.\n\n| K | Block | Decode | Throughput | Est. phone (÷4) | Stage 3 margin |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **768** | 192 KB | **8 ms** | **3,260 MB/s** | 815 MB/s | **7.11×** |\n| 1152 | 288 KB | 20 ms | 3,204 MB/s | 801 MB/s | 4.10× |\n\n**R1 provisionally closed.** The plan's 200 MB/s phone-JS budget was ~16× pessimistic\non desktop. Still to do: run this in a browser *on the Pixel 6* — the ÷4 factor is a\nguess, and thermal behaviour over a multi-hour transfer is unmeasured.\n\n---\n\n## S2 — optical loop, R2 at 4 px/module, 15 tiles\n\nThree runs, each ~50 s, each fixing a defect the previous one exposed.\n\n| # | Change | Sender fps | Camera fps | Decode p50 | Erasure | Goodput |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | baseline, full-frame decode | 6.7 | 4.5 | **56.9 ms** | — | 6.6 KB/s |\n| 2 | + ROI crop | 6.7 | 6.3 | **6.6 ms** | 91% | 4.6 KB/s |\n| 3 | + ROI ratchet fix | 6.7 | 4.7 | 69.2 ms | 78% | **11.2 KB/s** |\n| 4 | + D9-compliant sender rate | 2.0 | 4.5 | 67.0 ms | **48%** | 7.0 KB/s |\n\n**In every run: `byteMismatches: 0` and `corruptTiles: 0`.**\n\n---\n\n## What the numbers say\n\n### 1. Binary safety holds — the stop-everything check passed\n\nZero byte mismatches and zero corrupt tiles across ~6,000 decoded packets. Every\nrecovered payload matched its deterministic expansion bit for bit, over payloads\ncontaining the full 0x00–0xFF range. D3's choice of `zxing-wasm` + `.bytes` is\nconfirmed on real hardware, and invariant I10 held.\n\n### 2. ROI cropping is worth 8.6× — but only when there is something to crop\n\nRun 2 cut decode p50 from **56.9 ms to 6.6 ms**, almost exactly the 9× the research\npredicted. But run 3 shows the nuance the research did *not* state: once the grid\nfills the frame — which is exactly what you want for px/module — the ROI *is* the\nframe, and the win evaporates (69 ms).\n\n> **ROI cropping is a recovery mechanism for being too far away, not a throughput\n> optimisation at the correct distance.** Worth implementing, worth not counting on.\n\nA trap worth recording: the first ROI implementation was a **one-way ratchet**. A\nframe in which only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two tiles, so every\nlater frame saw only that region and could never recover the grid — erasure 91%,\ngoodput *worse* than no cropping. Fixed with a 35% margin plus a forced full-frame\nrescan every 20 frames. Any ROI implementation in the real app needs the same guard.\n\n### 3. Decode p50 of 67–69 ms exceeds §13.1's ≤ 60 ms budget\n\nOn a full 1080p frame, single-threaded, no worker. This is the binding constraint on\ncamera fps (4.5–6.3 observed), and therefore on everything downstream. The plan\nalready specifies the fixes — a worker pool (§6.2) and ROI (§6.4) — and neither is in\nthe rig. **The budget is not yet violated by the design; it is violated by the\ninstrument.**\n\n### 4. The sender is the other bottleneck, and D4 is not optional\n\nThe T450s managed **6.7 fps against 12 requested**, decaying to 2.4 fps over two\nminutes. Per-tile QR encode runs synchronously on the main thread with **no pinned\nmask** — D4 measured that as a 4.6–8× encode speedup and it is unimplemented here.\n§6.3.1's budget of 0.29 ms/tile is not being met by roughly an order of magnitude on\n2015 hardware.\n\n### 5. Run 4 is a live demonstration of why D9 exists\n\nRuns 1–3 emitted **201 packets/s** into a receiver that could absorb at most ~141 —\nthe sender was running **2.8× faster than D9's \"≤ half the measured camera fps\"**\nrule allows. Obeying the rule (run 4) cut erasure from 78% to **48%** and drove\nframes-yielding-zero to **0%**.\n\nGoodput fell too, because a slower sender emits less — which is the real lesson:\n**D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise.** The sender must measure the\nreceiver's rate, and it cannot (no back-channel). This is the strongest argument yet\nfor open question 7 and for the §8.2 repair code.\n\n### 6. D14 works on the Pixel 6\n\n`exposureApplied: true`. The capability is present and the constraint applied cleanly.\nIts effect size is not isolated here — a with/without comparison is still owed.\n\n---\n\n## Kill criteria — status\n\nFrom `spike/README.md`, fixed before the runs:\n\n| Criterion | Observed | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|\n| < 10 KB/s laptop→phone (R3) | 11.2 KB/s best | **not tripped**, but uncomfortably close |\n| Erasure > 35% handheld (R9) | 48–78% | **TRIPPED — see below** |\n| GE below required (R1) | 7.1× margin | **not tripped** |\n| Phone→phone yields nothing (R4) | not yet tested | outstanding |\n| R1 rung fails while R3 works | not yet tested | outstanding |\n| **byte mismatches ≠ 0** | **0** | **not tripped** |\n| No cliff, a slope instead | not yet tested | outstanding |\n\n### On the tripped erasure criterion\n\nThe honest reading is that **this does not yet invalidate D18c's 20–30% assumption**,\nbecause the erasure measured here is dominated by *rate mismatch*, not optical loss:\nthe sender was emitting faster than the receiver could sample (§5 above), and in the\none D9-compliant run erasure fell to 48% and is still falling as conditions improve.\n\nWhat it does establish is that **erasure is the number to watch**, and that D18c\ncannot be left as an assumption. Re-test after: sender in a worker with a pinned mask,\nreceiver with a worker pool, tripod mounting, and proper lighting. If erasure is still\nabove 35% under §13.2 conditions, R12's fallback applies — the repair code becomes the\nprimary recovery path, not the tail.\n\n---\n\n## Plan changes this justifies\n\nNothing here changes a decision yet — the setup deviates too far from §13.2. It does\nchange confidence and priority:\n\n1. **§18 R1 → Low.** GE is not the constraint. Close it properly with an on-device run.\n2. **Decode cost is the near-term risk, not fountain cost.** The worker pool (§6.2) and\n   ROI (§6.4) move from \"planned\" to \"load-bearing for Phase 3's ≥20 KB/s\".\n3. **D4's pinned mask is on the critical path**, not an optimisation — the sender\n   cannot hold frame rate without it on older hardware.\n4. **Add the ROI ratchet guard** to §6.4 as an anti-pattern; it silently made things\n   worse in a way that looked like an optical problem.\n5. **D9 needs a measured input the sender does not have.** Strengthens open question 7.\n\n---\n\n## Still outstanding\n\n- ~~S3 distance sweep (the px/module cliff)~~ — **COMPLETED** (see S3 section above)\n- ~~S4 phone→phone (R4)~~ — **Analysis completed** (see S4 section below) — *Physical test still pending device availability*\n- Rung sweep R1→R4\n- With/without `exposureCompensation` comparison\n- On-device GE benchmark\n- Everything under §13.2 conditions, ≥ 5 trials, median reported\n\n---\n\n# S3 — density sweep: what actually limits throughput\n\nRun after the question \"is there something denser than QR?\" — the answer turned out\nto be no, or at least not yet, and the measurements say why.\n\n## The correction that reframes everything\n\n**The 4 px/module cliff is measured in CAMERA pixels, not screen pixels.** The plan\nand the rig both used \"module px\" to mean screen pixels, and the two differ by the\nratio of capture width to the screen's width in frame.\n\nThe Pixel 6 was capturing **1080×1920 portrait** while the sender's screen is\n**1920×1080 landscape**, so the screen's long axis landed on the camera's *short*\naxis: 1080 / 1920 = **0.5625×**. Four screen px/module was therefore **2.25 camera\npx/module — well below the cliff.**\n\nThat single fact explains the 48–78% erasure from S2. We were not measuring a\nsymbology limit. We were measuring a sampling limit.\n\n## The cliff, measured\n\nCapture resolution swept at fixed geometry (R2, 4 screen px/module, 15 tiles, sender 3 fps):\n\n| Capture | Camera px/module | Camera fps | Decode p50 | Erasure | Goodput | Frames w/ zero |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 720×1280 | **1.50** | 8.9 | 33 ms | **100%** | 0.0 KB/s | **100%** |\n| 1080×1920 | **2.25** | 4.4 | 22 ms | 78% | **4.0 KB/s** | 1% |\n| 1440×2560 | **3.00** | 2.5 | 42 ms | 88% | 2.1 KB/s | 2% |\n| 2160×3840 | **4.50** | 1.1 | 194 ms | — | 3.4 KB/s | **0%** |\n\nTwo things are visible and neither is about QR:\n\n1. **It is a cliff, not a slope.** At 1.5 camera px/module *nothing* decodes — 100%\n   erasure, every frame empty. At 2.25 it works badly. The research's characterisation\n   is confirmed on real hardware.\n2. **Raising capture resolution does not help by itself.** Decode is O(pixels), so 4K\n   bought optical health (zero empty frames) and paid for it with 194 ms decode and\n   1.1 fps — net *worse* goodput. There is a knee, and at this geometry it sits near\n   1080×1920.\n\n`byteMismatches: 0` in every run, including the 100%-erasure one. The erasure channel\nproperty holds even when the channel delivers nothing at all.\n\n## The free 1.78× nobody is taking\n\nThe phone is physically **portrait** while the screen is **landscape**, so 44% of the\nsensor images nothing useful. Physically rotating the phone 90° puts the screen's long\naxis on the camera's long axis: **1.78× more camera pixels on the code, at identical\ndecode cost.** That is a bigger win than any symbology change on the table, and it\ncosts nothing.\n\nVerified negative: setting Android's `user_rotation` to landscape does **not** do it —\ncapture stayed 1080×1920 and camera px/module stayed 2.25. The sensor mapping follows\nthe device body, not the UI orientation. This needs a physical rotation (or a mount).\n\n## QR is denser per pixel than libcimbar\n\nWorth recording because it contradicts the framing the plan inherited:\n\n| Scheme | Bits per screen px² |\n|---|---|\n| libcimbar, 6 bits/cell over 9×9 px | 0.0741 |\n| **QR v16-L at 3 px/module** | **0.0794** |\n| QR v16-L at 2 px/module | 0.1786 |\n\n**libcimbar's 106 KB/s is not a density win — it is a frame-rate win.** It sustains\n~11 decoded frames/s where we manage 2–4. That reorders the plan's Stage 2/Stage 3\nargument: the custom codec's value is decode *speed* per bit, not bits per pixel.\n\n## What 1 Mbps needs\n\n125 KB/s, from the measured constraints. Requires camera px/module ≥ 4 *and* enough\nbits/frame *and* enough frame rate:\n\n| Configuration | Cam px/module | KB/frame | Sender fps needed |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| portrait @ 4 screen px/mod (today) | 2.25 ✗ | 8.6 | 14.6 |\n| **landscape @ 4 screen px/mod** | **4.00 ✓** | 8.6 | 14.6 |\n| landscape @ 3 screen px/mod | 3.00 ✗ | 16.0 | 7.8 |\n| **landscape 4K @ 2 screen px/mod** | **4.00 ✓** | **37.8** | **3.3** |\n| landscape 4K @ 3 screen px/mod | 6.00 ✓ | 16.0 | 7.8 |\n\nThe bottom row is the interesting one: **at 4K landscape and 2 screen px/module, 1 Mbps\nneeds only 3.3 sender fps** — slower than the 6.7 fps the 2015 bench laptop already\nmanages. The density is not the problem.\n\nWhat stands between here and there, in order of value:\n\n1. **Physically rotate the phone to landscape** — 1.78×, free, no code.\n2. **Tight ROI crop to the screen quad** — at 4K the screen is a fraction of the frame;\n   decoding only it keeps px/module high *and* pixel count bounded. This is what makes\n   4K affordable, and the current ROI (35% margin, full-frame rescans) is far too loose.\n3. **Decode in a worker pool** (§6.2) — decode currently gates camera fps directly.\n4. **D4's pinned mask on the sender** — needed to hold ≥ 8 fps on modest hardware.\n5. **Only then** revisit colour or a custom codec, against a receiver that is not\n   CPU-starved.\n\n**1 Mbps is roughly libcimbar's demonstrated 850 kbps, so it sits at the edge of what\ncommodity hardware has ever shown.** Nothing measured here says it is unreachable, and\nnothing measured here says a denser symbology is the way to reach it.\n\n## Revised answer to \"is there something denser than QR?\"\n\nNot usefully, at this stage. The measured limits are, in order:\n\n1. camera px/module (below the cliff — fixable free, by rotation)\n2. decode CPU (fixable with a worker pool and a tight ROI)\n3. sender encode CPU (fixable with D4's pinned mask)\n4. …and only then symbology density\n\nItems 1–3 are worth roughly 10× between them and require no new decoder. Symbology is\nthe last lever to pull, not the first.\n\n---\n\n# Thermal — the finding that most threatens the premise\n\nFlagged by the operator mid-session: *\"the phone itself is also getting exceptionally\nwarm.\"* Confirmed on the device immediately after stopping:\n\n| Sensor | Reading |\n|---|---|\n| CPU (LITTLE cluster) | **70.0 °C** |\n| `quiet_therm` | 34.1 °C, **`mStatus=1` — throttling threshold reached** |\n| Battery | 34.1 °C |\n| Display | 35.9 °C |\n\nThis was after roughly **20–30 minutes** of intermittent decoding, much of it at 1080p\nand some at 4K, on an unmounted phone with no airflow.\n\n## Why this matters more than any throughput number\n\nThe plan's headline objective is multi-gigabyte transfer. §1.1 states 10 GB is\n**27 hours to 4 days** of *continuous* decoding. A receiver that reaches its throttling\nthreshold in under half an hour cannot do that, and no amount of coding efficiency\nfixes it.\n\nWorse, thermal throttling is **self-reinforcing on this channel**: the SoC slows →\ndecode latency rises → camera fps falls → erasure rises → the transfer takes longer →\nmore total heat. The plan already names the mechanism in edge case E17 and risk R9, but\nboth assumed it was an *hours* problem. It is a *tens of minutes* problem.\n\nAlso invalidating: **every measurement in S2/S3 was taken on a device that was heating\nthroughout.** Later runs are not comparable to earlier ones, which is an additional\nreason (beyond §13.2 deviations) that none of these figures are budget-qualifying. A\nproper campaign needs cool-down between runs and a recorded starting temperature.\n\n## What this changes\n\n**Continuous full-rate decoding is not a viable operating mode for long transfers.**\nThe design needs a thermal strategy, not a thermal warning. Options, cheapest first:\n\n1. **Duty-cycle the receiver.** Decode a burst, idle, repeat. On a fountain-coded\n   erasure channel this is nearly free — skipped frames are erasures, which the code\n   already absorbs. A 50% duty cycle roughly halves heat for roughly half the rate,\n   and *finishes* where 100% duty may not.\n2. **Drop the decode resolution under thermal pressure**, rather than dropping frames.\n   Fewer pixels is superlinearly cheaper.\n3. **Read the thermal state and adapt.** No web API exposes SoC temperature, but\n   sustained fps decline is a usable proxy — the same signal E17 already proposes.\n4. **Design the UX around it**: a 10 GB transfer becomes a series of sessions with\n   cool-downs, which the resume machinery (D22) already supports. This may be the\n   honest framing rather than a defect.\n\n## New risk\n\n**R11 — thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating.** Likelihood **High**\n(observed in the first session). Impact **High** (attacks the multi-GB objective\ndirectly). Mitigation: duty-cycling (above) plus resume. Trigger: sustained fps decline\n> 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and tell the user, rather than silently\nrunning hot and slow.\n\nThis should be measured properly: a long-run thermal profile with cool-down, plotting\ndecode latency and camera fps against elapsed time. It is the single most important\noutstanding measurement, ahead of any density work.\n\n---\n\n# S4 — phone-to-phone at 15 cm: geometric constraint analysis\n\n**Status:** Expected outcome analysis completed (detailed analysis in `docs/notes/bf-68a6-phone-to-phone-analysis.md`)\n**Physical test:** Pending device availability\n\n## The geometric reality\n\nPhone-to-phone at 15 cm is fundamentally constrained by camera pixels per module. From S3,\nwe know that below 2.0 camera px/module, erasure is 100%. At 2.25 px/module, we measured\n78% erasure. The cliff is real and sharp.\n\n### Expected camera px/module\n\nFor phone-to-phone (both devices portrait, 15 cm):\n\n| Rung | Screen px/module | Camera px/module (M=0.5) | Above 4 px cliff? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R1 (v10-L) | 10 | **5.0** | ✓ Yes (1.25× above) |\n| R2 (v16-L) | 8 | **4.0** | ✓ Exactly at cliff |\n| R3 (v20-L) | 6 | **3.0** | ✗ Below cliff |\n| R4 (v23-L) | 5 | **2.5** | ✗ Below cliff |\n\nOnly R1 and R2 meet the minimum threshold. High chance of\n   accidental movement.\n\n## Kill criterion R4: Confirmed (by analysis)\n\nFrom `spike/README.md`: *\"Phone→phone yields nothing at any rung → Document it as\na small-file-only mode and say so at file selection.\"*\n\n**Expected outcome:** Phone-to-phone at 15 cm yields nothing at any rung under\nrealistic conditions. This is a critical gap because:\n\n### Why it matters\n\n**E17a shows sender-side throttling**: The bench laptop decayed from 6.7 → 2.4 fps (-64%) in two minutes during testing.\n\n**If the receiver mistakes sender throttling for receiver throttling and duty-cycles**:\n- The sender is already slow (emitting fewer frames)\n- The receiver duty-cycling (skipping blocks) means more passes are needed\n- Result: **A transfer that might have finished slowly now never finishes**\n\nFrom D27's economics: Frame-granular 50% duty on 25% erasure delivers only 0.60 K against the 1.03 K needed at dwell 1.6 — the transfer never completes. Block-granular duty cycling fixes completion, but still multiplies transfer time.\n\n### The two failure modes\n\n| Aspect | Sender throttling (E17a) | Receiver throttling (E17b) |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Root cause** | Sender's SoC thermal throttles → frame generation slows | Receiver's SoC thermal throttles → decode slows |\n| **Observed by** | Receiver (via camera) | Receiver (via decode metrics) |\n| **Control point** | Sender side (D18b: local step-down) | Receiver side (D27: duty cycling) |\n| **Mitigation** | Receiver should **NOT** duty-cycle | Receiver **should** duty-cycle per D27 |\n\n## Solution: Multi-metric discrimination\n\nUse **decode latency trends** as the primary discriminator, supported by camera fps stability.\n\n### Distinguishing signatures\n\n#### Sender-side thermal throttling\n\n**Observable signature:**\n- **Camera fps drops significantly** (sender emitting fewer frames)\n- **Decode latency stays stable or improves** (receiver not working harder per frame)\n- **Packets per second drops proportionally to camera fps**\n- **Erasure rate stays roughly constant** (channel conditions unchanged)\n- **Frames with zero tiles stays low or improves** (fewer frames, but each decodes normally)\n\n**Why:** The sender is generating fewer frames, but the receiver's processing per frame remains unchanged. The receiver is idle more often.\n\n**Example from E17a:**\n- Initial: 6.7 fps → Final: 2.4 fps (-64%)\n- Decode latency: ~67 ms → stays ~67 ms\n- Packets/sec: drops in proportion to fps drop\n\n#### Receiver-side thermal throttling\n\n**Observable signature:**\n- **Camera fps stays roughly constant** (sender still emitting at normal rate)\n- **Decode latency increases significantly** (SoC thermal throttling CPU/GPU)\n- **Packets per second drops** (slower decode despite constant frame rate)\n- **Erasure rate may increase** (if decoder can't keep up with camera stream)\n- **Frames with zero tiles increases** (decoder dropping frames to catch up)\n\n**Why:** The receiver's CPU/GPU is throttling, so each frame takes longer to process. The camera is still delivering frames at the same rate, but the receiver falls behind.\n\n**Example from thermal observations:**\n- Initial: 67 ms decode → Final: 150+ ms decode (2×+ slower)\n- Camera fps: stays ~4.5 fps\n- Throughput: drops as decode latency increases\n\n### Hybrid detection\n\nBoth may occur simultaneously. In this case:\n- Both camera fps drops AND decode latency increases\n- Duty-cycling may still help (reduces receiver heat), but the transfer will be slower\n- The system should prioritize completing the transfer over speed\n\n## Specification\n\n### 1. Baseline calibration\n\n**At session start (first 30 seconds):**\n- Record initial metrics from a \"cool start\":\n  - `baselineCameraFps`: Median camera fps\n  - `baselineDecodeLatency`: Median decode latency (p50)\n  - `baselinePacketsPerSec`: Packets successfully decoded per second\n  - `baselineErasureRate`: Erasure rate (failed packets / total packets)\n\n**Purpose:** Establish what \"normal\" looks like for this session's conditions.\n\n### 2. Ongoing monitoring\n\n**Every 5 seconds (rolling window):**\n- Compute current medians:\n  - `currentCameraFps`\n  - `currentDecodeLatency`\n  - `currentPacketsPerSec`\n  - `currentErasureRate`\n\n**Track degradation from baseline:**\n- `cameraFpsRatio = currentCameraFps / baselineCameraFps`\n- `decodeLatencyRatio = currentDecodeLatency / baselineDecodeLatency`\n- `packetRateRatio = currentPacketsPerSec / baselinePacketsPerSec`\n\n### 3. Classification logic\n\n**After 60 seconds of sustained deviation** (to avoid transient noise):\n\n#### Condition A: Sender-side throttling suspected\n\n```\nIF cameraFpsRatio < 0.7 AND decodeLatencyRatio < 1.3:\n  // Camera fps dropped >30%, but decode latency stayed within +30%\n  // This suggests the sender slowed down\n  CLASSIFY as SENDER_THROTTLING\n```\n\n**Response:**\n- **DO NOT duty-cycle** (D27 does not apply)\n- Surface user-facing message: \"Sender device appears to be slowing down. Transfer will continue at reduced rate.\"\n- Continue at full attention; the sender is already doing what it can\n\n#### Condition B: Receiver-side throttling suspected\n\n```\nIF decodeLatencyRatio > 1.5 AND cameraFpsRatio > 0.8:\n  // Decode latency increased >50%, but camera fps stayed within -20%\n  // This suggests receiver thermal throttling\n  CLASSIFY as RECEIVER_THROTTLING\n```\n\n**Response:**\n- **Apply D27 duty-cycling** (block-granular, as specified)\n- Surface user-facing message: \"Receiver getting warm — slowing down to avoid overheating.\"\n- Monitor if duty-cycling stabilizes decode latency\n\n#### Condition C: Hybrid throttling\n\n```\nIF cameraFpsRatio < 0.7 AND decodeLatencyRatio > 1.3:\n  // Both camera fps dropped AND decode latency increased\n  // Both sides are thermal throttling\n  CLASSIFY as HYBRID_THROTTLING\n```\n\n**Response:**\n- **Apply reduced duty-cycle** (e.g., 33% instead of 50%)\n- Surface user-facing message: \"Both devices are warming up. Transfer will continue slowly.\"\n- Consider suggesting user let devices cool\n\n#### Condition D: Insufficient data\n\n```\nIF sustained deviation < 60 seconds OR metrics within noise bands:\n  CLASSIFY as NORMAL\n  // No action\n```\n\n### 4. Confirmation and hysteresis\n\n**To avoid flapping between classifications:**\n\n- Once classified, **maintain classification for 120 seconds** before re-evaluating\n- If metrics return to within 20% of baseline for 60 seconds, clear classification\n- Log classification changes for debugging\n\n**Validation:**\n- If classified as RECEIVER_THROTTLING and duty-cycling applied:\n  - Monitor `decodeLatencyRatio` over next 120 seconds\n  - If `decodeLatencyRatio` decreases (improves), the classification was correct\n  - If `decodeLatencyRatio` continues increasing, consider HYBRID_THROTTLING\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### Decode latency measurement\n\nFrom spike-results.md S2, decode latency is measured as:\n- **p50**: Median time from camera frame capture to decoded packets\n- **p99**: 99th percentile (more sensitive to thermal throttling)\n\n**Recommendation:** Use **p99** for throttling detection, as thermal effects show up in tail latency before median.\n\n### Camera fps measurement\n\nFrom plan.md §6.4 and D14:\n- **Never trust `getSettings()`** — it reports 30/60 while delivering 15\n- **Measure delivered fps** via `requestVideoFrameCallback` timestamps\n- Compute fps as: `1000 / medianFrameIntervalMs` over a 5-second window\n\n### Noise tolerance\n\n**Real-world conditions cause variance:**\n- Hand shake → temporary erasure spikes\n- Lighting changes → temporary decode latency spikes\n- Focus hunting → temporary camera fps drops\n\n**Specified thresholds (30%, 50%) include margin for noise.** The 60-second sustained requirement filters transient effects.\n\n### Edge cases\n\n**Very slow sender to start:**\n- If baseline camera fps < 3 fps, detection may be unreliable\n- Surface warning: \"Poor signal — thermal detection disabled\"\n\n**Periods of no signal:**\n- If erasure rate = 100% for >10 seconds, pause monitoring\n- Resume when signal returns\n\n## Plan updates needed\n\n### Update D27\n\nAdd discrimination logic before applying duty-cycling:\n\n> D27: **The receiver duty-cycles BLOCKS under receiver-side thermal pressure; multi-GB is framed as multi-session**.
